item.statement: The reciprocating wear behavior of the alloy has not yet been examined in previous studies.
quotes: Only few studies have been carried out to examine the wear behaviour at elevated temperature.
The sliding wear behaviour in the pin-on-disc test at temperatures of up to 900 °C was investigated.
The reciprocating wear behaviour still needs to be examined.

item.statement: There is an initial decrease in wear resistance at moderate temperatures before it improves at higher temperatures.
quotes: With an increase in temperature from room temperature to 500 °C, a slight increase in the wear depth occurs, indicating a reduced wear resistance.
A further increase in test temperature resulted in a distinct increase in the wear resistance.
With increasing temperature, initially a slight decrease in the wear resistance occurred up to a temperature of 650 °C.

item.statement: Higher temperatures lead to better wear resistance but result in a high standard deviation of the coefficient of friction due to interrupted oxide layers.
quotes: Due to the formation of an interrupted oxide layer, a high standard deviation of the COF occurs.
The surface of the sample tested at a temperature of 650 °C is also incompletely covered with oxides.
With a further increase in the test temperature, the content of the surface covered with oxides gradually increases.
